paper.title: FlexSP: Accelerating Large Language Model Training via Flexible Sequence Parallelism

reading.scope: Physical pages 2–13 and 17: design, evaluation and selected appendices; pages 14–16 bibliography are locators only. Abstract page was read in the earlier screening phase.

findings.finding: Variable-length training and packing need sequence boundaries, causal masks and positions; Ulysses attention sequence/head all-to-all is not the Megatron SP definition.

Joint modeled placement uses both total tokens and squared lengths, memory limits and communication. Bucketed lengths, restricted group choices and a small set of microbatch candidates limit any optimality claim.

Communication group pools and CPU planning overlap reduce exposed preparation. Solver latency remains seconds; the 64-to-1024 GPU optimization study estimates training time and is not a 1024-GPU training measurement.

Measured experiments use 64 A100 40GB GPUs, eight per node and 400Gb/s interconnect. GPT models use learned position embeddings, contributing 1–2B parameters at the longest setting; they are not Qwen3 RoPE/GQA models.
Appendix lists CP integration as future work. Checkpoint and fitting-error descriptions are configuration-specific and not universal accuracy or compatibility guarantees.

prior_abstract_screening.reason: FlexSP 针对训练序列长度不均选择 SP 分散方式，候选对应第 6／10 章；尚未读完整代价模型、重分组代价或核实公开框架集成。

editorial_decision.placement: 10.2.3, existing experiment 10-3 and figure 10-3 variable-length variant; no new core section.

scope: Selected primary reading and independent arithmetic only; no downloaded code, model, simulator or hardware execution.
paper_to_framework_gap: Official FlexSP branch b4666892601f1adab345dbf07b6af2c300eb7c90 is separate from current Galvatron main. Training coefficients and bandwidths are GPT/A100-specific; memory budget and solver timeout are explicit code settings.
Selected transformer code expands GQA K/V before Ulysses communication. Native model KV head count alone does not determine transmitted payload.
Selected cross-entropy and pipeline files do not close final valid-token and distributed-gradient normalization; no correctness bug is inferred.
